activities.description: Jerry Travis introduces a feature of Windows 11 called 'Memory Integrity'.
He searches for 'windows security' in the Windows search bar.
He attempts to turn on 'Memory Integrity'.

characterInteraction.description: As a still image on the intro screen.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Relevant for users who need to enable security features in Windows 11.

narrativeProgression.description: The scene introduces the topic and demonstrates how to locate the 'Memory Integrity' setting.
A notification pops up stating that Memory Integrity can't be turned on due to incompatible drivers. This creates suspense and leads into the next scene.

props.name: Laptop with a backlit keyboard (intro screen only)

scenes.title: Introduction to Memory Integrity

videoEditingDetails.description: Intro screen with Jerry Travis's image and website address.

activities.description: Jerry Travis reveals he has incompatible drivers.
He identifies the incompatible drivers as leftover from a software-defined radio setup.
He selects 'View' and then 'Devices by driver'.
He locates the incompatible driver in the list.
He right-clicks on the driver and selects 'Uninstall device'.
He checks the box to 'Attempt to remove the driver while it is in use'.
He goes back to the 'Core isolation' settings and scans again.
'Memory Integrity' is now enabled, and a restart is required to apply the changes.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Useful for troubleshooting and technical education for Windows 11 users.

narrativeProgression.description: The scene focuses on identifying and removing the incompatible drivers blocking the 'Memory Integrity' feature.
The problem is solved, and the goal of enabling 'Memory Integrity' is achieved.
